explanation: Establishes exact soundness and completeness of the physical residue join. The actual stored buckets provide both directions of the residue-equality characterization for original index pairs.
theorem_title: Exact membership in the constructed wanted-pair list
theorem_formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.WantedPairs.mem_pairs {μ : ℕ → ℤ} {offsets flat NR NL M i j : ℕ} {left right : ℕ → ℕ}
    (H : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.Stored μ right NR M offsets flat) (hl : ∀ a < NL, left a < M)
    (hr : ∀ b < NR, right b < M) :
    (i,j) ∈ _root_.ThreeSum.WantedPairs.pairs μ offsets flat left NL ↔ i < NL ∧ j < NR ∧ right j=left i := by sorry
theorem_natural_language_statement:
Let actual stored right buckets represent a residue-key function on $N_R$ indices, with all right keys below $M$, and let the $N_L$ left keys also be below $M$. Then $$ (i,j)\in\operatorname{pairs}\iff i<N_L\land j<N_R\land q_R(j)=q_L(i).$$

Establishes exact soundness and completeness of the physical residue join. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
